reasoning: B is the narrow winner, mainly because its RL design is sounder and closer to the brief. Set B keeps the stated project shape: a circular tank, survival time as the fish score, a single learning predator, and an explicit co-evolution/self-play ladder (fixed opponents → naive co-learning → opponent pool, with saved generations, cross-play and ratings). Each environment teaches its concept as a ladder of rungs: tabular → DQN → CNN for Snake, REINFORCE → PPO for the fish. It keeps truncation separate from termination, adds ablations and a corridor sanity world, and has very concrete golden cases (closed-form GAE, the clipped objective, returns-to-go, physics). Its M1 is a true vertical slice that includes replay and the library reference. B's weaknesses: stale history kept in the documents (the brief's 'For Snake, the first environment' and 'Not doing: Designing future environments now' while the spec designs all three; AD-09/AD-13 'adopted before M1 is built'; a risk citing 'TC-01–TC-49' when there are 71 cases; replan notes); M2 and M3 have no Exit criteria; claims are left to 'the skill chooses the test', a looser oracle; and it freezes helper maths functions in the contract. Set A has stronger roadmap and statistics rigor: every milestone has checkable Exits, a precisely specified paired permutation test with Holm correction, and hand-derived check-world gates. But it drifts from the ground truth: a square tank, fish scored by hits with respawn, 2 predators, and no self-play or past-opponent mechanism for the co-evolution concept. It also splits Snake so that M1 has no replay viewer and only a weak online-Q spine, leaving 'see/check/explain' as a layer-like M2. Its pipelines list alternative world and baseline classes as sequential steps, and it keeps routed/assumed open questions that are already settled. Packets in both sets omit some types the builder needs, at similar rates.
